name: nm45
question: Does the league, re-trained on the fixed seating code with players who never fold in its pool, keep nm25's win rate against calling stations while staying as hard to exploit as nm25?
why: nm44 (the league) passed four of five checks and failed against the calling station: a paired difference of -27.4 bb/100 [-29.2, -25.6] on seed 13, the same on seeds 14 and 15 (docs/2026-11-23-review-and-plan.md, section 5), about a fifth of nm25's +126 win against it. The league trains mostly against strong players who fold correctly, so it learns to bluff and value-bet thin against them; a station punishes that. nm44 also cut the rule players' share from nm25's 0.5 to 0.4 and trained on the seating bug (B1: 8.7% of opponent seats on empty chairs), both fixed here. Two other findings set the checks: the old other-players rule compared a point estimate with 1.0 bb/100 and had no interval (A2), and nm25's 30-minute exploiter reads +0.75 mean over four seeds (+1.1, +0.8, +0.4, +0.7; SD 0.29), not the single +0.2 earlier limits came from (A1).

checks.why: it must not lose to nm25 in nm25's own game

the check nm44 failed, now paired: on the same deals as nm25, the 95% interval of the difference must lie above -2.0 bb/100 against every rule player, so a station gap like nm44's is ruled out, not merely unseen. At 100,000 hands the station interval is about +/-0.8, so a network level with nm25 passes about 998 times in 1,000
the league's purpose: at least as good as nm25 on average across 25 generated players, and never far behind (unchanged from nm44)
bluff jams and raises must lose prize equity against it, as against nm25

judged on the mean of four seeds, as nm25's +0.75 was measured (A1); the limit is that plus 0.5, about two and a half standard errors of a difference of two four-seed means. nm43 (+1.32) would fail it, nm44 (+0.50) would pass
a report for the reviewer: where nm45 decides differently from nm25, especially facing bets
